subject: BlueSpruce - throughput collapse after v6b quant switch (urgent)
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@bluespruce.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@bluespruce.ai
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 09:12:34 -0700
Subject: Immediate: severe throughput collapse after v6b quant switch

Karthik —

We pushed the v6b quant profile yesterday morning (per your team’s recommendation). Since ~02:00 UTC we’re seeing a 60-80% drop in successful token throughput on our high-volume routes and a sharp rise in 5xx errors. This is customer-impacting — web checkout timeouts, background scoring jobs failing repeatedly.

Attached are a condensed set of traces and an error-sample file (error-samples.txt). Can you confirm this is the v6b quant profile in Redwood's public catalog that you advised? We need urgent remediation and a timeline. Our CTO, Caroline, is asking for an exec-level update.

—Daniel
Daniel Park
Head of Engineering, BlueSpruce Analytics
Daniel.Park@bluespruce.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@bluespruce.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 Jun 2028 11:05:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Immediate: severe throughput collapse after v6b quant switch

Daniel — thanks for the quick note and for attaching telemetry. We see the file and I’ve looped in Monica (SRE lead on Dedicated customers) and Lauren (Customer Success for BlueSpruce).

Initial read: the traces show sudden CPU/GPU context-switch spikes and a marked increase in kernel fallback paths consistent with the new int8 qprofile we shipped as v6b. Monica — can you confirm whether v6b was marked compatible with BlueSpruce’s instance family (A100 80GB private pool) in the rollout matrix?

Short answers for BlueSpruce:
- We’ll prioritize an immediate rollback to the prior v6a profile for your routes (if you approve).
- We’ll request temporary burst capacity on Redwood Dedicated to keep latency below SLA while we sort this.
- We’ll prepare an executive note for Caroline and your leadership with timeline and compensation options.

Daniel — can you confirm a maintenance window if needed? I’d like to avoid any partial mitigation that causes more errors.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 Jun 2028 08:30:05 -07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: severe throughput collapse after v6b quant switch

Karthik / Lauren — I pulled the rollout logs overnight. BlueSpruce was on the v6b qprofile via a targeted rollout at 2028-06-28T01:10Z. The profile was marked "recommended" for xlarge A100-80B in the catalog, but there is a known differentiation: v6b enables an experimental kernel-path that triggers on sequences >512 with certain kv-cache patterns. BlueSpruce traffic has a heavy tail >512.

Telemetry summary (high level):
- P95 latency: 210ms -> 620ms after switch
- Token throughput (successful tokens/sec): -72% on /v1/generate-hotpath
- 5xx rate: 0.2% -> 3.8%
- Kernel fallback (%) increased from 2% -> 42% on affected hosts

I’ve staged a rollback playbook (playbook-rollback-v6b.pdf) that will revert the qprofile and flush affected caches; rollback is expected to restore baseline within 10-20 minutes per host. Risk: partial rollback while heterogeneous hosts remain may cause transient increases in errors — recommendation is a coordinated cutover during a short window.

I’ve attached a tar with the critical traces for your ops team.

—Monica
Monica Patel
SRE Lead, Redwood Dedicated Customers
monica.patel@redwood.ai

-----Attachment: playbook-rollback-v6b.pdf-----

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 01 Jul 2028 10:14:44 -07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: severe throughput collapse after v6b quant switch

Short and tactical:
- I recommend we authorize immediate rollback to v6a for BlueSpruce routes. Monica’s playbook looks good. Rolling back + cache flush should cut p95 back to ~230ms in the hotpath.
- Offer BlueSpruce a one-week credit and a follow-up performance audit (free) while we run a post-mortem.
- For execs: we should escalate to CTO-level standby (Marissa and Aditya) and include Caroline in the loop.

Operational asks for the rollback:
1) BlueSpruce confirm a 20-minute maintenance window in next 2 hours.
2) Redwood ops to enable temporary burst capacity to keep error amplification low.
3) Post-rollback QA: run canonical prompt set for 30 minutes; send results to BlueSpruce.

If we don't get maintenance window, we can do rolling rollback with stricter circuit breakers — but that risks transient 5xx spikes.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Serving Reliability, Redwood Inference

Daniel / Caroline —

Thank you for the quick signal and the telemetry. We’re authorizing an immediate rollback to v6a for your customer routes and will execute per Monica’s playbook in a scheduled 20‑minute maintenance window at 19:15 Pacific today (UTC 02:15).

What to expect:
- Rollback + kv-cache flush across affected hosts (tracked by playbook). Estimated restoration: 10-20 minutes after start; we’ll monitor and post status to this thread.
- Temporary burst capacity applied during the window to reduce cascading failures.
- A one-week credit applied to your account (HS-84219) as a remediation gesture; we’ll follow up with a formal exec note with compensation options and timeline for a post-mortem.

Please reply here to confirm the 19:15 PT window. If you prefer earlier, we can shift — ops is standing by.

—Karthik
